rv.q: Kokandy Productions' intense, committed new staging of the iconic 1968 musical "Hair" is not so much an exploration of the Age of Aquarius as a manifestation of an age of anxiety.

This show gets the work’s seriousness, and plumbs its continuing relevancies with great effectiveness, particularly in its fever dream of Act 2 where we see one example after another of imperial destruction.
This revival of HAIR is one for the Chicago books.
The show is infectious, and you leave it feeling loopy and swingy, with your hair a little longer.

Removed from its era, what stands out most about Hair is its joyous, irresistible depiction of the political fervor and boundless optimism of the young: youth determined to affect social change by whatever means they have at hand.
Kokandy's production makes it clear that that message is just as important today.
Kokandy’s Hair elevates the best moments of the material without allowing the more dated ones to overstay their welcome.
Kokandy Productions delivers an energetic and visually engaging revival of Hair that embraces the musical's enduring message of peace, love, and individuality.
In the end, while this may not be your grandfather's 'Hair,' Kokandy still delivers a powerful, resonant message.
The overall performance was entertaining and exhilarating.
The production feels a little long-winded, especially during Act II, which wears out its welcome long before the conclusion.
Just think, over 60 years later you can see how history can repeats itself ( or not), in this slick production that Kokandy Productions has dusted off for our viewing pleasure.
The Kokandy cast, as always, delivers on vocal quality and has put their own spin on this now classic musical.
The cast delivers the score with phenomenal singing talent, but the rest of the production felt sparse and ungrounded.

cn.t: Kokandy's revival earns mostly positive reviews for its talented cast and vibrant energy, though critics are divided on whether the Gen Z update successfully grounds the '60s counterculture classic in modern relevance.
